summary: Northwestern beat Rutgers 42-14. Chiles and the rushing attack powered the offense, and takeaways helped the defense. Oregon changed offensive coordinators before Saturday’s matchup.

items.headline: Northwestern beats Rutgers 42-14
items.tldr: The Wildcats earned their sixth win with a fast start. Watch whether the opening script can keep creating useful downs when the next defense adjusts.

items.headline: Chiles accounts for five touchdowns against Rutgers
items.tldr: Three passing scores and two rushing scores gave the offense different ways to finish. Watch how the quarterback’s run threat changes the edge defender’s assignment.

items.headline: The rushing attack produces 283 yards
items.tldr: Inside NU traces the ground game’s role in the win. Keep the blocking, quarterback read and runner’s first cut connected before looking for the breakaway.

items.headline: Raymond’s 46-yard touchdown leaves run-defense work
items.tldr: Rutgers cut the margin to 28-14 on the long carry and a two-point conversion. Keep the edge and pursuit connected before the next runner reaches open space.

items.headline: Oregon dismisses offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer
items.tldr: The Ducks announced the change Sunday before hosting Northwestern. Prepare for possible adjustments without assuming a new play-caller will change every formation.

lead.headline: Keep the quarterback’s choices open.
lead.body: Make the edge defender account for the handoff, keeper and pass. On defense, get lined up early and preserve assignments while Oregon works through its offensive change.

matchup.thesis: Trust the read and the assignment
matchup.question: What should fans watch in the next game?
matchup.answer: Keep the run action convincing without making every down depend on a quarterback escape. Defend what the formation shows, then communicate through motion before the snap.

signals.summary: Make pressure produce a hard throw
signals.detail: Close the pocket while preserving coverage behind it. Finish a sound defensive down even when the chance for an interception does not arrive.
